You are a product analyst doing a COMPREHENSIVE gap analysis of the Nxeon hosting platform to find what's MISSING or half-built. Read-only (no edits). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 + Prisma + a Node worker; products: VPS, shared hosting, game servers, business email, domains, NxCloud/Nextcloud, free tools, an AI site builder). It's a Hostinger-style multi-product host.

Your job: produce a PRIORITIZED, SPECIFIC list of feature GAPS — things a competitive host has that Nxeon lacks, features that are stubbed/half-built, and obvious missing capabilities. Ground every item in the codebase (cite file/dir) — don't hand-wave.

Investigate across the product surface:
- **Per-product completeness**: for VPS, hosting, game, email, domains, NxCloud — does each have the full expected feature set vs Hostinger/OVH/cPanel? (e.g. VPS: snapshots, ISO mount, reverse DNS, firewall UI, monitoring/graphs, OS reinstall, rescue mode; hosting: staging sites, git deploy, cron UI, email routing, DNS editor, one-click SSL, malware scan UI, phpMyAdmin-equivalent (note: DB Studio exists), backup restore UI; email: catch-all, aliases, autoresponders, spam controls, webmail; domains: transfers, WHOIS privacy, DNSSEC, bulk, auto-renew UI).
- **Billing/account**: invoices PDF, tax/VAT handling, multiple currencies, account credit/refunds UI, usage-based alerts, spending caps, downgrade/cancel flows, dunning UX, receipts.
- **Customer experience**: onboarding wizard, dashboard empty states, notifications/alerts (email + in-app), status page, uptime monitoring for customer services, mobile responsiveness, dark/light, search, help/docs in-context.
- **Trust/ops**: 2FA enforcement options, audit log for the customer, SSO, team/role granularity, API completeness (only /api/v1/servers exists?), webhooks for customers, a public status page.
- **Admin/internal**: what operational tooling is missing (fleet health, capacity planning, abuse handling, refund tooling, coupon analytics, churn metrics).
- **Growth**: affiliate dashboard depth, referral UX, reviews/testimonials pipeline (note: don't fabricate), knowledge base/blog gaps.

For EACH gap: a short title, WHY it matters (customer/revenue impact), current state (what exists in the code / what's missing, with a file or dir reference), effort estimate (S/M/L), and whether it's buildable now vs gated (needs external access/hardware). Rank by impact×feasibility. Group by product area. Aim for the 20-30 highest-value real gaps, not an exhaustive nitpick list. Return as markdown. Report to orchestrator — findings only, no preamble. Do NOT edit files.

I have enough grounding across all product areas. Here is the gap analysis.

---

# Nxeon Platform — Feature Gap Analysis

Scope: read-only pass over `/opt/nxeon` (135 Prisma models, ~80 `lib/actions-*` modules, 28 worker jobs). Nxeon is unusually complete for its stage — VPS snapshots/backups/metrics/console/OS-reinstall, hosting cron+DB-Studio+SSL+file-manager, full email (aliases/autoresponder/forwarding/webmail/sieve), domain transfers/WHOIS-privacy/registrar-lock all exist. The gaps below are the real holes vs a Hostinger/OVH/cPanel-class competitor, ranked by impact × feasibility.

## Top priorities (do these first)

| # | Gap | Area | Effort | Buildable now? |
|---|-----|------|--------|----------------|
| 1 | VAT/tax computed but never charged | Billing | M | Yes |
| 2 | No real PDF invoices | Billing | M | Yes |
| 3 | No self-serve cancel/terminate | Billing | M | Yes |
| 4 | Public API is one read-only endpoint | API/Trust | L | Yes |
| 5 | No firewall UI for VPS | VPS | M | Yes |
| 6 | No dedicated game control panel | Game | L | Yes |

---

## Billing & Account (highest revenue/compliance impact)

**1. Tax/VAT is display-only, never actually charged — S/M to wire, HIGH impact.**
`lib/tax.ts` header literally states: *"multi-currency here is DISPLAY ONLY … Tax helpers likewise compute a display/quote breakdown; wiring them [into charges is not done]."* VAT/GST is shown in quotes but Stripe charges the pre-tax amount. This is a compliance and revenue problem in any EU/UK sale. Current state: `applyTax`, `taxRate` exist but aren't in the `lib/stripe.ts` / `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` charge path. Buildable now.

**2. No real PDF invoices.** `lib/mailer.ts:90` — *"There is no PDF library installed (and we can't add dependencies), so we attach the branded print-ready invoice HTML."* Customers get HTML and must Print→Save-as-PDF (`lib/invoices.ts:379`). Every competitor emails a real PDF; accounting departments require it. Effort M (add a renderer or server-side print). Buildable.

**3. No self-serve cancellation/termination flow.** No `cancelServer`/`terminateServer`/`requestCancel` action exists in `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts` or `-extra.ts` — only `resizeServerDown` (downgrade). Cancellation appears to be support-ticket driven. This drives support load and, in some jurisdictions, is legally required to be self-serve. Effort M. Buildable.

**4. No spending caps / usage alerts.** `lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts` has only `saveAutoRecharge`. No budget threshold, no "you've spent $X" alert, no hard spend cap. Wallet-based billing makes runaway spend a real churn/chargeback risk. Effort S/M. Buildable.

**5. Multi-currency is cosmetic.** `lib/tax.ts` — `formatMoney` swaps the symbol but does **no FX conversion**; EUR/GBP prices are just USD numbers with a € sign. Either remove the currency selector or add real FX. Effort M. Buildable.

## VPS (feature parity vs OVH/Contabo)

**6. No firewall UI.** `components/customer/NetworkingControls.tsx` exposes only NAT port-forwarding (`addPortForward`/`deletePortForward`). No inbound firewall rule editor / security-group concept. Effort M. Buildable (iptables/proxmox fw).

**7. No rescue mode.** No rescue-boot action anywhere in `lib/proxmox.ts` or `lib/actions-server-*`. Standard on every VPS host for "I broke SSH." Effort M. Partially gated (needs a rescue image on nodes).

**8. No ISO mount / custom ISO boot.** `reinstallToOs` (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`) covers stock templates only; no attach-ISO. Effort M. Gated on ISO storage.

**9. No reverse DNS (PTR) UI.** `lib/ovh.ts` has `setReverse` but it's never surfaced to customers. Note: many plans are NAT VPS behind a shared IP, so this only matters for dedicated-IP customers (`lib/dedicated-ip.ts`). Effort S. Buildable for dedicated-IP holders.

*(Snapshots, backups+restore, metrics graphs `MetricsPanel.tsx`, noVNC console, OS reinstall all present — no gap.)*

## Shared Hosting

**10. No staging environments.** `lib/actions-hosting.ts` has addon domains, subdomains, cron, DB, backups, PHP-version, WordPress install — but no clone-to-staging / push-to-live. (The "staging" in `worker/hosting.ts` refers to *node* provisioning, not customer site staging.) Hostinger/cPanel ship this. Effort M. Buildable.

**11. No git deploy.** No git clone/pull/webhook-deploy in hosting actions or `worker/hosting.ts`. Developers expect push-to-deploy. Effort M. Buildable.

**12. No customer-facing malware scan UI.** ClamAV + ModSecurity run at node-hardening level (`worker/hosting.ts:618`) but there's no per-account scan button / results view (Imunify-style). Effort S/M. Buildable (surface existing ClamAV).
